body:
The latest tech M&A deals includes announcements on SpaceX, Uber Technologies, ezCater, KKR, Harness, and others.

SpaceX to Acquire Nationwide 800 MHz Spectrum Portfolio from Grain Management

SpaceX has signed a definitive agreement to acquire 100 percent of Grain Management’s nationwide 800 MHz spectrum portfolio, expanding the wireless frequencies available for satellite direct-to-device connectivity. The transaction, announced October 8, is subject to Federal Communications Commission approval and customary closing conditions. Grain acquired the spectrum portfolio from T-Mobile in August 2026 through a transaction involving cash and its 600 MHz spectrum holdings. SpaceX intends to use the frequencies to expand Starlink Mobile services connecting ordinary mobile devices through satellite infrastructure. BDT & MSD Partners advised Grain financially, while Milbank provided legal counsel and Latham & Watkins handled regulatory matters. Financial consideration was not disclosed.

Uber Agrees $2.3 Billion Acquisition of Corporate Catering Platform ezCater

Uber Technologies has agreed to acquire ezCater for approximately $2.3 billion, expanding its position in corporate food ordering and workplace catering. Boston-based ezCater operates a technology marketplace connecting businesses with restaurants and catering providers for employee meals, meetings and corporate events. The transaction adds specialised enterprise ordering capabilities to Uber’s existing food-delivery and business-services operations. ezCater’s platform supports scheduled catering, group orders, administrative controls and business purchasing workflows. The acquisition gives Uber access to additional corporate customers and restaurant relationships beyond conventional consumer delivery. The reported transaction value is approximately $2.3 billion. Detailed financing arrangements, regulatory conditions and the expected closing date were not specified in the available transaction information.

KKR Agrees $5.1 Billion Acquisition of Gen II Fund Services

KKR has agreed to acquire Gen II Fund Services in a transaction valued at approximately $5.1 billion including debt, expanding its exposure to technology-enabled financial administration. New York-based Gen II provides fund accounting, tax, compliance and administrative services to private-capital investment managers. Its operating infrastructure supports more than 12,000 entities across private equity, private credit, infrastructure and real estate. The sellers are investor groups led by Hg and General Atlantic, which invested in the business in 2020. KKR manages approximately $796 billion in assets, including around $255 billion in private equity. The transaction adds a financial-services operating business with recurring institutional relationships and substantial regulatory and reporting requirements.

Harness Acquires Augment Code AI Assets to Expand Autonomous Software Development

Harness has acquired selected technology assets from Augment Code, adding AI-assisted software engineering capabilities to its autonomous development platform. The October 8 transaction covers Cosmos, the Auggie command-line interface, the Code Context Engine and related technology, with the associated engineering team joining Harness. The acquisition is an asset transaction rather than a purchase of the entire Augment Code company. Cosmos will become the Harness Cosmos Software Factory Agent, connecting AI-generated code with testing, security, deployment and production operations. Harness serves enterprise customers including United Airlines, Morningstar and Choice Hotels. The acquired technology will operate alongside Harness agents for software delivery, runtime protection and cloud-cost management. Financial terms were not disclosed.
